_comment: Curated models.dev MetadataID -> entity-tuple OVERRIDE table for the metadata<->entity join (metadata_join.go). It is consulted FIRST and takes PRECEDENCE over the mechanical decomposition (curated > mechanical, matching the parse/ curated-overrides and ollama_aliases.json precedents). A models.dev metadata id is lab-scoped ('<lab>/<model>', e.g. 'zhipuai/glm-4.6'); the mechanical join strips the '<lab>/' prefix, decomposes the remainder through the production parse pipeline (ParseFamilyDetailed + ParseParamSize) into an EntityRef key, and matches that key against the catalog entity set. An alias is needed precisely where the mechanical key MISSES the catalog (family present but tuple mismatch -> otherwise reported in modelsdev_unlinked.json) or matches the WRONG entity, so the curator can re-map the metadata id onto the intended identity. KEYING: keys are lowercased MetadataID strings. Each value is an explicit entity tuple: 'family' (canonical, lowercase), optional 'variant', optional 'version', optional 'param_size' (canonical ParseParamSize token, e.g. '70b'), and optional 'modifier' (the IDENTITY-class modifier list, EntityModifiers projection). Keys MUST be kept sorted. This file is hand-curated seed data; no tool rewrites it. It ships EMPTY: the initial alias set is discovered from real join misses over the vendored models.dev snapshot (see the codegen-emitted modelsdev_unlinked.json report) and added here as those disagreements are triaged. Example row shape (illustrative, not active): "somelab/some-model-70b": {"family": "llama", "version": "3.3", "param_size": "70b", "modifier": ["instruct"]}. COLLISION HAZARD — do NOT alias a metadata id onto an entity that already carries another row's metadata or that conflates several distinct lab models under one coarse key: the last write wins, so aliasing silently OVERWRITES or MISATTRIBUTES metadata. Three currently-unlinked rows are known-unsafe to alias under today's decomposition and are intentionally left in modelsdev_unlinked.json awaiting entity-granularity work (a tracked deferral): google/gemini-omni-flash-preview (collapses onto gemini/flash, already held by google/gemini-flash-latest), poolside/laguna-xs-2.1 (collapses onto laguna, shared with poolside/laguna-xs.2 + poolside/laguna-m.1), and openai/gpt-realtime-2.1 (collapses onto the bare gpt family entity). Only nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5 has a distinct empty target (nemotron/v1.5@3.3) and is aliased below.
